findings.title: Each refinement round discards all subsolver work on prior disjuncts (pop/re-assert is quadratic and drops learned clauses)
findings.detail: lazyCheckStar (lines 536-558) now does pop(); push(); assertFormula(not(D_1 or ... or D_k)) every round that found new disjuncts. In cvc5 a user pop removes everything user-context-dependent above the popped level: the CNF clauses and SAT/theory state for the previous refined formula, and SolverEngine::pop() additionally calls d_smtSolver->getPreprocessor()->clearLearnedLiterals() (solver_engine.cpp:2249). So each round re-preprocesses and re-CNFs the entire cumulative disjunction from scratch: total preprocessing/clausification work over k rounds is O(k^2) in the number of disjuncts, versus O(k) for the old scheme which asserted only the new disjunct's negation each round and let the incremental subsolver retain all clauses and learned facts about previously covered regions. Only the base predicate (level-1) preprocessing is reused. This is the deliberate tradeoff stated in the new header comment (bounded live assertions / per-assertion caches), but be aware it can be a net pessimization when the number of refinement rounds is large, since the SAT solver re-derives the structure of all previous disjuncts on every round. Not a correctness bug.

findings.title: Subsolver bookkeeping (sub.negated/sub.covered/sub.pushed) can desync from engine state if pop/push/assert throws
findings.detail: In the new block (lines 538-557), sub.covered is extended and sub.negated set to pairs.size() before the engine calls, and sub.pushed is only updated after assertFormula succeeds. If sub.engine->pop() succeeds but sub.engine->push() or assertFormula() then throws (e.g. an interrupt, or a ModalException), sub.pushed remains true while the engine has no pushed frame; a later re-entry into lazyCheckStar for this lambda would then call pop() with d_userLevels empty and hit ContextManager::userPop()'s ModalException("Cannot pop beyond the first user frame") (context_manager.cpp:108-111). Conversely, if push() succeeds and assertFormula throws, the next round pops a frame whose refined formula was never asserted while sub.negated already claims those disjuncts were handled (the old per-disjunct loop had the same negated-counter exposure but no pushed-frame invariant to break). This only matters if the exception is caught above LiaStarExtension and the same SolverEngine instance is re-driven (e.g. an outer incremental check-sat after a recoverable error or interrupt); in the common case the exception aborts the whole solve and the state is never reused. Cheap hardening: set sub.pushed = false immediately after the pop() and move sub.negated = pairs.size() after the assertFormula call.

findings.title: Subsolver bookkeeping committed before pop/push/assert leaves inconsistent state if an engine call throws
findings.detail: In lazyCheckStar (lines 537-559), the new code commits sub.covered (lines 547-549) and sub.negated (line 551) BEFORE the engine sequence pop()/push()/assertFormula(), while sub.pushed is only set after assertFormula succeeds (line 558). The old code set sub.negated only after all assertFormula calls, so a throw merely caused benign re-assertion on retry. With the new ordering, if any of the three engine calls throws and the embedding catches the exception and continues solving (incremental API usage; LiaStarExtension and its d_subsolvers persist across check-sats inside TheoryArith), the Subsolver is left permanently inconsistent in one of these ways: (a) pop() succeeds but push() throws: sub.pushed stays true with zero user frames, so the next refinement round's sub.engine->pop() raises ModalException "Cannot pop beyond the first user frame" (src/smt/context_manager.cpp:111) -- note ContextManager::userPop also flips SmtMode via d_state.notifyUserPush() before performing that check, so even the failed pop mutates state; (b) push() succeeds but assertFormula throws on the first refinement (sub.pushed still false): the next round pushes again without popping, permanently leaking an empty user frame; (c) in every throw case, sub.negated has already advanced past the unasserted disjuncts, so until a new disjunct arrives the block at line 537 is skipped and lazyHilbert's checkSat runs WITHOUT the newest refinement, letting getDisjunct rediscover an already-covered cell -- addCone then appends a duplicate cone to d_lazyCones and getStarConstraints mints a duplicate set of star skolems and constraints (bloat and wasted rounds, though not unsoundness, and it self-heals once the duplicate forces the block to re-run). Mitigating factors keeping this minor: the subsolver has its own Options/Env/ResourceManager (no resource-limit or interrupt exceptions propagate into it), so an exception in pop/push/assertFormula essentially indicates an internal error, and in the common embedding the exception propagates out of checkFullEffort and aborts the query anyway. A simple hardening is to perform pop() (setting sub.pushed=false immediately), then push()+assertFormula, and only then advance sub.negated / set sub.pushed=true (folding into a local Node first, assigning sub.covered last).

result.reasoning:
Every load-bearing claim in the finding reproduces concretely from the code, and the behavior is introduced by this diff (HEAD never popped).

1. The new loop is as described. /home/mudathir/all/cvc5/mudathir/src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp lines 536-558: when new disjuncts arrived, it folds them into the cumulative `sub.covered` OR, then does `if (sub.pushed) sub.engine->pop(); sub.engine->push(); sub.engine->assertFormula(sub.covered.notNode());`. The old code at HEAD (verified via `git show HEAD:...`, lines ~533-543) asserted only `disjunct.notNode()` per new disjunct with no push/pop, so the subsolver retained all prior clauses and learned facts.

2. Pop really discards the prior round's work, exactly as claimed:
   - SolverEngine::pop() (src/smt/solver_engine.cpp:2242-2255) calls `d_smtSolver->getPreprocessor()->clearLearnedLiterals()` at exactly line 2249, as cited.
   - CnfStream's node-to-literal caches are context-dependent maps on the user context (src/prop/cnf_stream.cpp:41-42, constructed with `userContext` in src/prop/prop_engine.cpp:86-91), so the literal mappings for all disjuncts converted inside the popped frame are removed.
   - Minisat's user pop (src/prop/minisat/core/Solver.cc:1937-1987) calls `removeClausesAboveLevel` on both `clauses_persistent` and `clauses_removable` (lines 1972-1973); `clauses_removable` includes learned clauses, so learned clauses tied to the popped frame are physically deleted.

3. The quadratic asymptotics hold. In incremental mode, SmtDriverSingleCall::getNextAssertions (src/smt/smt_driver.cpp:204-215) feeds only assertions added since the last check (`d_assertionListIndex` is a CDO on the user context, restored on pop). Old scheme: each `not(D_i)` preprocessed/CNF-converted once, O(k) total over k rounds. New scheme: round k pops the frame containing `not(D_1 or ... or D_{k-1})` (erasing its CNF/SAT state) and asserts the brand-new node `not(D_1 or ... or D_k)` of size O(k) (lazyHilbert adds ~1 disjunct per round via getDisjunct/addCone), which must be fully re-preprocessed and re-clausified since the caches for its subterms were popped. Total O(k^2). Only the base predicate, asserted in getSubsolver (liastar_extension.cpp:507) before any push, survives pops, as the reviewer notes.

4. The subsolver is exercised every round: lazyHilbert -> LiaStarUtils::getDisjunct (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_utils.cpp:626-642) does checkSat + getValue, so the dropped SAT/preprocessing state is re-derived each round, not hypothetically.

Caveats consistent with the finding's own framing: it is a performance concern, not a correctness bug, and it is the deliberate tradeoff documented in the new Subsolver header comment (bounded live assertions vs. re-derivation). But the finding's specific technical content -- pop/re-assert makes total preprocessing/clausification work quadratic in the number of disjuncts, drops learned clauses and preprocessor learned literals every round, and only the base-level work is reused -- is accurate, newly introduced by this diff, and triggers on every run with more than one refinement round. So it is a real (performance) problem worth flagging, exactly as characterized.

The claim's mechanics are structurally accurate (sub.negated/sub.covered updated before engine calls at liastar_extension.cpp:536-558, sub.pushed set only after assertFormula, and ContextManager::userPop at context_manager.cpp:109-111 throws ModalException when d_userLevels is empty), but the triggering exception is not concretely reachable. In the critical window (after pop() succeeds, before sub.pushed=true): (a) sub.engine->push() cannot throw — notifyUserPush throws only when not incremental, and getSubsolver unconditionally sets incremental=true (liastar_extension.cpp:476); refreshAssertions has no new assertions to preprocess since covered.notNode() is asserted after the push; (b) assertFormula throws only via ensureWellFormedTerm on free variables (assertion builds), and sub.covered is fully substituted into skolem space by construction (getDisjunct builds disjuncts from atoms of skolem-space sub.base and the from/to mapping is complete); logic-legality checks are deferred to checkSat time, which occurs in lazyHilbert after sub.pushed=true where bookkeeping is consistent; (c) the cited "interrupt" does not exist as an exception path — ResourceManager::spendResource never throws (resource_manager.cpp:201, it notifies listeners and checks return unknown), theory::Interrupted is thrown only at main-theory output-channel safePoints (none in this window) and is caught inside TheoryEngine::check, and there is no UnsafeInterruptException in this codebase; the subsolver also has its own fresh ResourceManager with no limits. The re-drive precondition also fails: SmtDriver::checkSat catches only LogicException/TypeCheckingExceptionPrivate and rethrows; plain ModalException is non-recoverable at the API boundary and fatal in the main driver, so no supported path re-enters lazyCheckStar after such an exception. The only remaining throws are std::bad_alloc or debug-build AssertionException, after which cvc5 makes no usability guarantees anyway. The assertFormula-throws variant additionally self-heals because sub.covered is cumulative, and the reviewer concedes the negated-counter exposure pre-existed. The suggested hardening (set sub.pushed=false after pop, move sub.negated after assertFormula) is cheap and harmless as defensive style, but the finding is hypothetical-but-impossible rather than a real problem introduced by the diff.

The ordering facts are accurately described: in lazyCheckStar (liastar_extension.cpp:537-559) sub.covered and sub.negated are committed before the pop()/push()/assertFormula() sequence and sub.pushed is set after, whereas the old code set sub.negated after all assertFormula calls and used no frames (a mid-loop throw was benign). ContextManager::userPop (context_manager.cpp:104-121) does throw ModalException when no user frames exist. However, the trigger — one of the three engine calls throwing AND the embedding continuing to solve on the same solver — cannot be reproduced concretely: (1) pop() throws only if sub.pushed is true with zero user frames, a state that itself presupposes a prior failure (circular precondition); (2) push() = beginCall (no-op after init; subsolver has its own default Options/ResourceManager, so no resource/interrupt exceptions) + refreshAssertions (preprocesses an empty pending-assertion delta, since the previous round's assertions were processed by getDisjunct's checkSat and the pop removed the frame) + userPush (no throw path); (3) assertFormula throws only via ensureWellFormedTerm on free variables (assertion builds), and the asserted node is the negation of an OR of exactly the same skolem-space disjuncts the old code asserted individually — any such throw is pre-existing, not introduced. The only remaining sources are std::bad_alloc or internal AssertionException, i.e., internal errors. Nothing in cvc5 catches and continues from an exception in checkFullEffort: theory_engine.cpp catches only theory::Interrupted; smt_driver.cpp:95-111 catches LogicException/TypeCheckingExceptionPrivate but rethrows (and neither can arise from these three calls). The exception escapes the main solver's checkSat, after which the main solver's own internal state has no continued-use guarantee, so the persistent-Subsolver-corruption scenario requires unsupported continue-after-internal-error usage. The reviewer's own mitigating-factors paragraph concedes the trigger is essentially an internal error that aborts the query. The suggested reorder is reasonable hardening, but the finding is hypothetical-but-effectively-impossible rather than a real problem introduced by the diff.

findings.title: sub.negated advanced before the subsolver is refined: an exception mid-refinement permanently skips asserting not(covered)
findings.detail: In lazyCheckStar (lines 536-558), 'sub.negated = pairs.size();' executes BEFORE 'sub.engine->pop(); sub.engine->push(); sub.engine->assertFormula(sub.covered.notNode());'. If any of those engine calls throws (interrupt, memory-out, an exception from push()'s refreshAssertions/preprocessing), the exception propagates out of checkFullEffort, but sub.negated has already been advanced to pairs.size(). On the next refinement round the guard 'if (sub.negated < pairs.size())' is then false (skip case), so the new not(covered) is never asserted and lazyHilbert runs against a subsolver that is missing the latest refined formula (after a pop-then-throw it may even be missing ALL negated disjuncts, holding only the base predicate). getDisjunct then re-enumerates already-covered cells, and addCone appends duplicate cones (wasted Hilbert-basis computations and redundant star constraints; the literal may never reach 'complete'). The committed baseline did not have this hazard: it set sub.negated only AFTER the per-disjunct assertFormula loop, so a failed round was simply retried (re-asserting a negation twice is harmless, silently skipping it is not). Fix: perform pop/push/assertFormula first and update sub.negated/sub.pushed last (re-folding the same disjunct into covered on retry is logically harmless), or update the bookkeeping only after the assert succeeds. Note this is exception-path-only; in the normal path the new bookkeeping is exactly equivalent to the old one (verified by code comparison against HEAD and by regression/incremental stress tests, which all pass).

findings.title: Each refinement round re-preprocesses the entire growing disjunction and discards all subsolver learning, making cumulative refinement cost quadratic
findings.detail: The new scheme in lazyCheckStar asserts a brand-new formula not(d_1 or ... or d_k) every round in a fresh frame. Although the live-assertion count is now constant (the stated rationale), the asserted node is new each round, so the subsolver must re-preprocess and re-clausify O(k) disjuncts on round k, giving O(k^2) cumulative preprocessing/CNF work over k rounds, versus O(k) total for the old one-assertFormula-per-new-disjunct scheme (where each not(d_i) was processed exactly once and stayed asserted). In addition, SolverEngine::pop() (src/smt/solver_engine.cpp:2242) clears the preprocessor's learned literals, and the user-context pop discards the SAT solver's clauses for the popped frame each round, so conflict clauses derived from not(covered) (which logically remain valid, since the new refined formula implies the old one) are relearned from scratch every round. For predicates with many convex cells this can be a significant slowdown relative to the committed baseline. This is a performance regression risk only, not a correctness bug; the refinement logic itself was verified equivalent (sub.covered folds exactly the nodes the old loop negated, with identical skolem substitution; the base predicate below the first user frame survives every pop; the skip case leaves the subsolver in exactly the {base, not(covered)} state lazyHilbert expects; multi-literal/shared-lambda and incremental main-solver push/pop scenarios produce correct sat/unsat answers in testing). A middle ground would be to keep the old per-disjunct assertions within the single pushed frame and only rebuild the frame when assertion count crosses a threshold.

result.reasoning: Every load-bearing claim reproduces concretely from the code. (1) The new lazyCheckStar (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:537-559) does pop/push/assert of a brand-new node not(d_1 or ... or d_k) on every round that discovered new disjuncts, and the lazy loop runs one round per convex cell until complete, with addCone growing pairs each productive round — so the rebuild fires nearly every round and round k's formula has k disjuncts. (2) Quadratic re-preprocessing is real: SmtDriverSingleCall::getNextAssertions (src/smt/smt_driver.cpp:205-215) tracks already-processed assertions via d_assertionListIndex, a CDO in the user context, and the assertion list itself is a user-context CDList — SolverEngine::pop() rewinds both, so the next checkSat fully re-preprocesses the O(k)-sized refined formula; the old scheme (no push/pop, one assertFormula per new disjunct) preprocessed each not(d_i) exactly once, O(k) total vs O(k^2) cumulative. (3) CNF work is also redone: CnfStream's d_nodeToLiteralMap/d_literalToNodeMap/d_booleanVariables are context-dependent structures on the user context (src/prop/prop_engine.cpp:86-91, src/prop/cnf_stream.cpp:38-42), so the popped frame's Tseitin definitions for the disjunction are discarded each round, and Solver::pop destroys the frame's SAT variables via resizeVars. (4) SolverEngine::pop() at src/smt/solver_engine.cpp:2242 calls clearLearnedLiterals() (line 2249), exactly as the review cites. (5) MiniSat's Solver::pop (src/prop/minisat/core/Solver.cc:1937-1987) removes clauses above the new assertion level from both clauses_persistent and clauses_removable; learnt clauses are allocated at the max user level of their derivation (Solver.cc:1535), so conflict clauses derived from the frame's not(covered) clauses are deleted on every pop despite being logically implied by the next round's stronger formula. The problem is introduced by the diff (the baseline never pushed/popped the subsolver and never re-asserted old disjuncts) and is not hypothetical (many-cell predicates driving many rounds are the feature's target workload). The reviewer's framing is also accurate in its limits: it is a performance regression risk, not a correctness bug — the refinement logic, the skip-round state, and the base assertion surviving pops all check out. The only soft spot is magnitude (per-round checkSat may dominate the quadratic preprocessing term, and rewriter attribute caching amortizes some rewriting), but the review already hedges this appropriately ("risk", "can be a significant slowdown"), so the finding stands as a real, code-grounded trade-off the diff's rationale does not account for.

The structural reading is accurate: in the new code (liastar_extension.cpp:537-559) 'sub.negated = pairs.size()' executes before pop()/push()/assertFormula(covered.notNode()), whereas HEAD updated sub.negated only after the assertFormula loop; the guard 'if (sub.negated < pairs.size())' would skip re-asserting after a mid-window throw, and d_subsolvers persists across checkSat calls. However, adversarial verification shows the triggering scenario is not concretely reachable. (1) Interrupt: the subsolver is a raw SolverEngine with fresh default Options (getSubsolver, line 473), not registered with the parent's resource manager and never interrupt()ed; main-solver interrupts manifest as theory::Interrupted thrown from TheoryEngine's own spendResource/interrupt checks, and the critical window contains no such calls, so the only in-process catch-and-continue path (catch(theory::Interrupted) in theory_engine.cpp:618) cannot fire there. (2) Preprocessing exceptions in push(): on round 1 the guard is false (d_lazyCones[lambda] is empty until addCone runs in lazyHilbert), so the base predicate is preprocessed at getDisjunct's checkSat, outside the window and identically in old and new code; on later rounds nothing unpreprocessed is pending at push() time (the previous covered assertion was preprocessed at the prior checkSat and removed by pop(); the new one is asserted after push and preprocessed at the next checkSat). Deterministic exceptions therefore strike only where the new bookkeeping is already consistent, and recur identically on retry in both versions. (3) Memory-out: bad_alloc could strike inside the window, but SmtDriver::checkSat resets the SAT trail only for LogicException/TypeCheckingExceptionPrivate (smt_driver.cpp:95-111); after any other exception the main solver is left mid-search with unbalanced beginCall/endCall, so the subsequent successful checkSat that the scenario requires is not a supported execution. Even granting the scenario, the consequence is bounded: a missing refinement only makes the subsolver more satisfiable, so 'complete' (subsolver UNSAT) cannot be reached spuriously (no unsoundness); in the assertFormula-throw case the duplicate disjunct grows pairs, the guard turns true next round, and the up-to-date covered is asserted (one wasted round, then self-correction); in the pop-then-push-throw case the next refinement throws ModalException('Cannot pop beyond the first user frame', context_manager.cpp:111), a loud failure rather than the claimed silent never-completing loop. This is at most optional exception-safety hardening (update bookkeeping after the engine calls), not a real reachable problem introduced by the diff.
